newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt support solid but lags combined opposition.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt support solid but lags combined opposition.

text.p: Less than three weeks from New Zealand's general election, polling continues to show solid support for the ruling National Party, but the three main opposition parties would be able to topple the conservative government if they worked together.

A three-poll rolling average of party support in the most recent polls shows National averaging 38.5 percent, Labour 18.7 percent, economic nationalist New Zealand First 17.3 percent, and the five party left wing Alliance grouping 13.7 percent.

In the most recent poll conducted for the New Zealand Herald by Waikato University and published on Saturday, the conservative National Party was up three points on a similar poll a week before at 39.6 percent.
Prime Minister Jim Bolger said in his campaign opening speech last week that National would need to win more than 40 percent of the vote to be returned to office.
Among the opposition parties Labour was steady on 17 percent support, the New Zealand First Party was down one to 18 percent, and the Alliance won 15 percent support, up one.
National's likely coalition partners, the Christian Coalition and free market ACT New Zealand, each scored four percent support.

The three poll rolling average shows ACT on 3.8 percent and the Christian Coalition on 5.1 percent. Under the mixed member proportional representation system adopted by New Zealand for the October 12 election a party must win five percent of the party vote to qualify for seats if it does not win one of the 65 electorates.
If the Herald poll was translated into seats in the House National would have 53 MPs, New Zealand First 24, Labour 23 and the Alliance 20.
A total of 850 people nationwide were interviewed by telephone for the poll between September 11 and 18.
